## **Tomato [टोमॅटो]**

**Climate [हवामान]**

Although tomato [टोमॅटो] crops can be grown throughout the year, considering the temperature [तापमान] of the climate [हवामान] while planting can certainly increase production [उत्पादन]. Seed germination [बियाणे अंकुरण] and plant growth [वाढ] are best in temperatures ranging from 16°C to 29°C. A temperature [तापमान] of 18°C to 32°C is very suitable for fruit setting [फळधारणा]. If the temperature [तापमान] rises above 32°C, it has an adverse effect on fruit setting [फळधारणा].

**Soil [माती]**

Tomato [टोमॅटो] crops can be grown in light [प्रकाश] to heavy soils. Generally, the crop [पीक] matures early in light [प्रकाश] soils and late in heavy soils. It grows well in medium to black soils with good drainage or in loamy soils. The soil pH [मृदा सामू] should be between 6 and 7.5. The soil [माती] in which tomato [टोमॅटो] crop [पीक] is to be grown should not have had brinjal [वांगे], chili and potato [बटाटा] crops in the previous season, as this leads to a higher incidence of pests and diseases.

**Improved Varieties**

Various varieties of tomatoes are available in straight and hybrid types. Mahatma Phule Agricultural University has released Dhanashree and Bhagyashree in the straight type for nearby to medium-sized markets and Phule Raja and Phule Suvarna in the hybrid type for distant markets, and Phule Kesari, which is rich in beta-carotene. Also, Phule Jayashree variety of cherry [चेरी] tomato [टोमॅटो] has been released. Similarly, many hybrid varieties of private seed [बियाणे] companies are available in the market. Tomato [टोमॅटो] can be planted in all three seasons. For Kharif season [खरीप हंगाम], sowing [पेरणी] should be done in the nursery [रोपवाटिका] in May-June, for Rabi season [रबी हंगाम] in September-October and for summer season [उन्हाळी हंगाम] in January-February.

This symptom [लक्षण] is seen on the leaves of crops such as tobacco [तंबाखू], okra [भेंडी], tomato [टोमॅटो], papaya [पपई], etc. In okra [भेंडी], the veins turn yellow. - **Leaf Curl [पाने मुरडणे]:** The leaves of chili peppers become curled and crumpled. Hence, it is called Leaf Curl [पाने मुरडणे] disease [रोग]. The leaves of eggplants become small. Fruit set [फळधारण] does not occur as usual. Diseased fruits develop.
- **Bunchy Top [पर्णगुच्छ]:** This is called Bunchy Top [पर्णगुच्छ] of Banana [केळी] in English. The growth [वाढ] of the banana [केळी] plant is stunted, and the plant becomes dwarfed. Yellowish spots appear on the leaves. If bananas develop, the fruits are small and tasteless.
- **Tristeza:** This disease [रोग] affects citrus. Shoots and branches wither. The harmful inoculum is spread by aphids [मापकीड] and the 'Citrus psyllid [सायला]' insect [कीटक].

**Barnyard Millet [भगर/वरई]/Varai Cultivation Technology**

In Maharashtra, Barnyard Millet [भगर/वरई]/Varai is an important crop [पीक] in the nutritious millet [भरडधान्य] category. This crop [पीक] is mainly cultivated in the high rainfall areas of the Western Ghat region, sub-mountainous region, and hilly areas of the Konkan region. For the tribal and local farmers of this region, finger millet [नाचणी] is a major nutritious millet [भरडधान्य] crop [पीक]. It is cultivated in Nashik, Akole (Ahmednagar), Nandurbar, Pune, Kolhapur, Satara, Dhule districts of the state as well as Palghar, Raigad, Ratnagiri, Sindhudurg districts of Konkan region. Varai grains [धान्ये] are mainly eaten as a major food for fasting. Considering the dietary importance of Varai/Varai crop [पीक], the religious importance of Varai crop [पीक] and the nutritional components in it, it is appropriate to call this grain [धान्य] a nutritious grain [धान्य]. Varai grain [धान्य] has a balanced and higher proportion of fat, fiber, minerals [खनिजे] and iron [लोह]. Eating Varai rice [बासमती तांदूळ]/bhakari during fasting does not cause any kind of acidity [आम्लता]. Therefore, Varai is beneficial for health [आरोग्य]. Varai rice [बासमती तांदूळ], bhakari, biscuits, ladoos, vermicelli, chakli, shev etc. are made from Varai. Climate [हवामान] Varai/Varai crop [पीक] is grown in warm and temperate regions with annual rainfall up to 2500 mm from sea level up to 1000 to 1800 meters. A maximum temperature [तापमान] of 250 to 270 °C is conducive for the growth [वाढ] of this crop [पीक].

**Soil [माती]**

**[Animal Health and Nutrition Extension](MANAGE, Hyderabad)**
```
Demonstration Projects and Pilot Programs Demonstration farms and pilot programs are valuable for showcasing best practices and new technologies. These serve as proof-of-concept sites where farmers can see the results of implementing new methods. Examples of demonstration projects might include: Integrated Pest Management [एकात्मिक कीड व्यवस्थापन]: A farm may demonstrate the use of biological control [जैविक नियंत्रण] methods instead of chemical pesticides [रासायनिक कीटकनाशके]. Climate-Smart Practices [हवामान सुसंगत पद्धती]: Demonstration farms may adopt drought [दुष्काळ]-tolerant crops or water-efficient irrigation techniques [पाणी-कार्यक्षम सिंचन तंत्र] to showcase how climate [हवामान]-resilient practices can boost farm productivity [शेती उत्पादकता]. 3. Adoption of Farm Management [शेती व्यवस्थापन] Practices Once extension strategies have been implemented, the next challenge is ensuring that farmers adopt and maintain these new practices. Key areas of farm management [शेती व्यवस्थापन] where adoption is crucial include: Improved Crop [पीक] and Livestock Management [पशुधन व्यवस्थापन] Efficient management [व्यवस्थापन] of crops and livestock [पशुधन] is essential for improving productivity. Key practices include: Crop Rotation [पीक फेरपालट] and Intercropping [आंतरपीक]: These techniques help in maintaining soil health [मृदा आरोग्य], managing pests, and optimizing yields. Livestock Health [पशुधन आरोग्य] and Genetics: Providing farmers with knowledge on animal husbandry [पशुसंवर्धन], disease prevention [रोग प्रतिबंध], and breeding [प्रजनन] techniques helps ensure healthy livestock [निरोगी जनावर]. Sustainable Soil [माती] and Water Management [पाण्याचे व्यवस्थापन]: Techniques like conservation tillage [संवर्धन मशागत], organic farming [सेंद्रिय शेती], and rainwater harvesting [पावसाचे पाणी साठवणे] can help ensure long-term productivity.
```

```
Aluminum phosphide and methyl bromide are restricted use pesticides

| Dry [कोरडे] Fruit, Cashew [काजू] Spices [मसाले] & Oil Seeds | Red Flour Beetle | Airtight | 24-32 gm / m3 | 24Hours and wait for minimum of 72 Hour |

**Follow the following five formulas to safely store grains [धान्ये] and seeds.**

- Dry [कोरडे] seeds / grains [धान्ये] in the sun (less than 8 percent moisture) and store in a well-ventilated place.
- Use a bamboo [बांबू] or polythene plinth to store seeds/grains [धान्ये].
- Use modern airtight warehouses for seed [बियाणे]/grain storage [धान्य साठवण].
- Use fumigant [धुरीकरण] insecticides [कीटकनाशके] for pest control [कीड नियंत्रण].
- Use poisoned bait to control rats in the field [शेत]. For this, mix 380 grams of crushed wheat [गहू]/sorghum [ज्वारी]/maize [मका] grains [धान्ये] + 10 ml of edible oil (groundnut [भुईमुग] or flaxseed oil) + 10 grams of zinc [झिंक] phosphide 80% powder well with a stick [काठी] in a pot, and make small 10-gram [हरभरा] balls of such poisonous bait. Fill them in plastic bags, seal them, and place a plastic 10-gram [हरभरा] bait bag in a burrow (hole). Approximately 10 grams of zinc [झिंक] phosphide powder is sufficient for 40 burrows in the field [शेत].

**Scientific and Trade Names of Recommended Insecticides [कीटकनाशके]**
```

**Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth**
```
The cultivation method, climate [हवामान], fertilizers, interculture, sowing method [बियाणे पेरण्याची पद्धत] and crop planning [पीक नियोजन] of this type of maize [मका] should be done in the same way as other maize [मका].

### **Management [व्यवस्थापन] of Pests and Diseases on Maize [मका]**

**Pests:**

1. **Aphids [मापकीड] and Leafhoppers [तुडतुडे]:**Measures - 1) Carry out deep ploughing [खोल नांगरणी] and harrowing [वखरणी] in summer so that the pupae of the pests will be destroyed. 2) Practice crop rotation [पीक फेरपालट]. 3) Sow [मादी डुक्कर] the crop [पीक] as per the recommended time only. 4) Select pest [कीड] resistant varieties [प्रतिकारक वाण] for sowing [पेरणी]. 5) Use chemical fertilizers [रासायनिक खते] in a balanced way. 6) Do not allow water stress [पाण्याचा ताण] to occur during the critical stages of crop [पीक] growth [वाढ]. 7) No labelled claim chemical insecticide [कीटकनाशक] is available for the management [व्यवस्थापन] of these pests.
2. **Stem Borer [खोड किउा]:**As soon as the infestation is seen after the crop [पीक] is about 30 days old, apply 3% granular Carbofuran [कार्बोफ्युरान] in the stem of the plant at the rate of 15 kg per hectare.
3. **American Armyworm [लष्करी अळी]:**Information on the control of this pest [कीड], disease [रोग] is under the heading Fall Armyworm [लष्करी अळी].
4. **Armyworm [लष्करी अळी] and Earhead Borer:**Follow the measures suggested for aphids [मापकीड] and leafhoppers [तुडतुडे] for the management [व्यवस्थापन] of these pests.
5. **Fall Army Worm (Spodoptera frugiperda):**This larva has an inverted 'Y' shaped mark on the front of its head. Pimply dark spots are seen on the body of the larva and small hairs are found in these spots

**Measures:** Follow the measures suggested for aphids [मापकीड] and leafhoppers [तुडतुडे] for the management [व्यवस्थापन] of these pests.

**Diseases:** Seedling mortality [रोपांची मर], stem rot, stalk rot, charcoal rot, leaf spot [पानांवरील ठिपके], rust [गंज रोग], and downy mildew [डाऊनी मिल्ड्यू] are the diseases found on maize [मका]. Take measures as per recommendation after observing the level of their incidence.
```

**Recent Advances in Diagnosis and Control of Livestock Diseases**
```
External Parasites [बाह्य परजीवी]: Integrated Pest Management [एकात्मिक कीड व्यवस्थापन]: Focusing on a combination of strategies, including chemical control [रासायनिक नियंत्रण] (insecticides [कीटकनाशके]), biological control [जैविक नियंत्रण], and cultural practices (sanitation, pasture management [चराई जमिनीचे व्यवस्थापन]) is key to effective control. Biological controls: Include any living organisms that kill the pests, such as other insects, animals, or fungi. Cultural controls include physical [शारीरिक तपासणी], mechanical or other preventative practices that reduce sites favourable for pest [कीड] development. Practices such as sanitation, water and manure management [खत व्यवस्थापन], and eliminating spoiled feed and silage [मुरघास], are common cultural controls used to help reduce pest [कीड] development sites. Chemical control [रासायनिक नियंत्रण] is a common method of controlling pests, but it is critical to understand the timing, mode of action [कृतीची पद्धत], and class of insecticide [कीटकनाशक] used. Determine whether the insecticide [कीटकनाशक] has long-term or short-term efficacy and consider withdrawal periods. Once producers implement control strategies, it's important to monitor pest [कीड] populations to determine whether management [व्यवस्थापन] efforts were effective. Pest [कीड] populations should also be monitored to determine if retreatment is needed. This includes assessing animal behaviour to see if they are less irritated and more comfortable.
```

**STANDARD VETERINARY TREATMENT GUIDELINES FOR LIVESTOCK AND POULTRY**
```
Treatment [उपचार] Antimicrobial therapy - as per the antimicrobial sensitivity test - under the supervision of the poultry [कुक्कुट] veterinarian [पशुवैद्यक] along with supportive therapy [सहायक उपचार] will reduce the losses in clinical infection [संसर्ग]. Strict withdrawal period should be followed after administration of antibiotics. Water sanitation and acidification of feed and water helps in prevention [प्रतिबंध]. Control Proper breeder [संकरक] farm and hatchery [अंडी उबवणूक केंद्र] hygiene [स्वच्छता] and sanitization. Feed hygiene [आहार स्वच्छता] and gut health management [आरोग्य व्यवस्थापन]. Prevention [प्रतिबंध]/Biosecurity [जैवसुरक्षा] Feed contamination with *E. coli* can be a source of infection [संसर्ग] for poultry [कुक्कुट]. Hence, it is advisable to use acidifiers (organic [सेंद्रिय] acids, pre- and pro-biotics (competitive exclusion)) and essential oils [आवश्यक तेल] as per recommended doses in the feed to maintain the gut integrity and reduce the *E. coli* contamination. Water hygiene [स्वच्छता] includes following steps: - Regular administration of water sanitizers such as Chlorine dioxide@0.2 ml/L - Use of water acidifiers to reduce the pH. - Regular removal of biofilms in the pipelines by using 10% H2 O2 . - Ensure regular care of clean drinking water [स्वच्छ पाणी देणे] pipes. - Rodent, insect [कीटक], and pest control [कीड नियंत्रण]. - Personal hygiene [स्वच्छता] of farm workers. - Avoiding open defecation in farm premises. - Regular cleaning [साफसफाई] and disinfection of poultry [कुक्कुट] sheds can help to reduce the environmental buildup of *E. coli.* Waste disposal in a poultry [कुक्कुट] farm is important to check further infection [संसर्ग]. Various steps include used poultry [कुक्कुट] litter [कचरा], carcasses, and other potentially contaminated farm waste should be transported and disposed of in a safe manner (deep burial, incineration or composting [खतनिर्मिती]) to prevent the direct or indirect exposure of humans, livestock [पशुधन] and wildlife to *E. coli*.
```

**[Animal Health and Nutrition Extension](MANAGE, Hyderabad)**
```
Public Private Partnership: Government should collaborate with private agencies like NGOs or organizations. This helps in promoting and developing affordable, efficient waste management [व्यवस्थापन] solutions to the farmers. *Government Schemes* *National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture [शाश्वत शेती] (NMSA)* Promotes sustainable agricultural practices [कृषी पद्धती] that improves productivity, soil health [मृदा आरोग्य] and water use efficiency [जल वापर कार्यक्षमता]. Helps in providing financial assistance up to 50% of cost for setting up vermicompost [गांडूळखत] units (5,000 per hac). *Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture [उद्यानविद्या] (MIDH)* Farming practices [शेती पद्धती] that improve soil fertility [मृदा सुपीकता] and reduce dependency on chemical fertilizers [रासायनिक खते]. Provides assistance to farmers up to 50% cost of vermicompost [गांडूळखत] units, up to a maximum of INR 50,000 per beneficiary. *National Food Security [अन्न सुरक्षा] Mission (NFSM)* promoting sustainable farming practices [शाश्वत शेती पद्धती] like vermicomposting [गांडूळ खत] and integrated pest management [एकात्मिक कीड व्यवस्थापन] to reduce dependency on chemical inputs and to enhance soil health [मृदा आरोग्य] and crop productivity [पीक उत्पादकता]. Provides financial assistance for the promotion of bio-fertilizer [जैविक खत]. *Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY)* Vermiculture [गांडूळ खत निर्मिती] and vermicomposting [गांडूळ खत], which are integral to organic farming [सेंद्रिय शेती], receive support as part of the scheme [योजना]'s goals to improve soil fertility [मृदा सुपीकता] and reduce chemical fertilizer [रासायनिक खत] use. *Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)* Aims to promote organic farming [सेंद्रिय शेती] through the adoption of traditional and eco-friendly farming practices [पर्यावरणपूरक शेती पद्धती]. PKVY focuses on enhancing the production [उत्पादन] of organic [सेंद्रिय] products, improving soil fertility [मृदा सुपीकता], reducing the dependence on chemical inputs, and promoting sustainable agricultural practices [कृषी पद्धती]. 5. Successful Case Studies of Vermi-Biotechnology [जैवतंत्रज्ञान]
```


----

**Krushi VNMAU**
```
The following points should be followed while managing the crop [पीक]

- Select crop [पीक] systems based on soil [माती] and rainfall.
- Crops like cotton [कापूस], tur, Kharif sorghum [ज्वारी], and soybean [सोयाबीन] should be taken in medium to heavy soils.
- In assured rainfall areas, dual cropping system [पीक प्रणाली] should be adopted for medium to heavy soils. It should include Moong-Rabi Sorghum [ज्वारी], Hybrid Sorghum [ज्वारी], Soybean [सोयाबीन] (in Kharif), and Safflower [करडई]/Chickpea [हरभरा] (in Rabi season [रबी हंगाम]) crops.
- Crops like Sunflower [सुर्यफुल], Tur, Bajra [बाजरी], Soybean [सोयाबीन], Sorghum [ज्वारी] should be taken in medium soils.
- Crops like Bajra [बाजरी], Kulthi, Sesame [तीळ], Niger, Castor [एरंड] should be taken in light [प्रकाश] soils.
- Intercropping [आंतरपीक] systems like hybrid sorghum [ज्वारी] + Tur (4:2), Bajra [बाजरी] + Tur (3:3), Soybean [सोयाबीन] + Tur (4:2), Cotton [कापूस] + Udid / Soybean [सोयाबीन] (1:1) cropping systems should be adopted.
- Contingency crop planning [पीक नियोजन] should be done as needed.
- Select early maturing varieties. Keep the proper amount of seeds and do seed treatment [बीज प्रक्रिया].
- Maintain the proper number of plants. For this, keep the proper distance between the two rows of crops and between the two plants.
- Carry out integrated nutrient management [एकात्मिक पोषण व्यवस्थापन] and integrated pest [कीड] and disease control [रोग नियंत्रण].
- Adopt integrated weed control [तण नियंत्रण] and carry out chemical weed control [तण नियंत्रण] and inter-cultivation at the right time.
- Sowing [पेरणी] of rabi crops [रब्बी पिके] should be done on time. Depending on the availability of moisture, proper tillage [जमिनीची मशागत] (zero tillage [जमिनीची मशागत] / minimum tillage [किमान मशागत] / general tillage [जमिनीची मशागत]) should be adopted.

**Objectives of Watershed Development Program**

1. To reduce soil erosion [जमीनीची धुप] caused by the flow of water over the land.
2. To percolate the rainwater that falls in the watershed area into the soil [माती].
3. To store the rainwater flowing from the land in the watershed at appropriate places.
4. To increase the groundwater storage [साठवण] in the watershed, to plant trees by digging ditches on sloping and barren lands.
5. To make efficient use of the water stored in the watershed.
6. To improve the degraded land in the watershed.
7. To maintain the balance of the environment in the watershed.
8. To improve the economic development of the people in the watershed and raise their living standards.

In order to achieve the various objectives of the watershed development program, the following measures of soil [माती] and water conservation [पाण्याचे संवर्धन] should be adopted according to the need, taking into account the land, crops, cropping systems, geology, streams, drains, etc. in the watershed.

1. Contour bunding [समोच्च बंधारे].
2. Graded bunding.
3. Terracing in highly sloping hilly areas.
4. Planting trees by digging ditches on sloping and barren lands.
5. Carrying out temporary or permanent treatments for gully control.
6. Creating farm ponds, village ponds, percolation [पाझरण] tanks, etc. for water storage [साठवण].
7. Nala straightening and nala bunding.
8. Building subsurface barriers.

Along with these protective and developmental measures of soil [माती] and water conservation [पाण्याचे संवर्धन], the following improved technology-related aspects should be adopted at the farm level.

1. Planting crops according to the classification of land.
2. Contour cultivation as well as biological bunding.
3. Adopting strip cropping [पट्टा शेती] method.
4. Conserved tillage [जमिनीची मशागत].
5. Agroforestry [कृषिवनशास्त्र], horticulture [उद्यानविद्या], and pasture [कुरण क्षेत्र] development.

7. Using high-quality seeds, fertilizers, and crop protection [पीक संरक्षण] measures.
8. Using protected irrigation [सिंचन] for dryland crops.

### **Which Crops Can Be Grown in a Greenhouse [हरितगृह]?**

Vegetables, fruits, flowers, and ornamental plants that have high market demand [बाजारातील मागणी] or are not readily available can mainly be grown in greenhouses from a commercial point of view. 7. Less water is required.

The main purpose of building a greenhouse [हरितगृह] is to create a favorable environment for crop [पीक] growth [वाढ]. It is necessary to build greenhouses that are easy, affordable, and economically viable for farmers, considering the geographical conditions. The method of using organic fertilizers [सेंद्रिय खते], green manures, bacterial fertilizers, and organic [सेंद्रिय] liquids in appropriate proportions as complementary fertilizers along with chemical fertilizers [रासायनिक खते] is called Integrated Nutrient Management [एकात्मिक पोषण व्यवस्थापन].

## **Crop Protection [पीक संरक्षण] without Chemical Insecticides [कीटकनाशके]**

The unwarranted and indiscriminate use of chemical insecticides [कीटकनाशके] for the control of pests on crops has led to resistance in pests, resurgence of harmful but previously suppressed pests, destruction of parasitoids and predators, and environmental pollution. # 3.1 Nursery [रोपवाटिका] Pond [तलाव] Preparation
Nursery [रोपवाटिका] pond [तलाव] preparation begins with making them free of weeds [तण] and predators and generating adequate natural food to ensure high rate of survival and good growth [वाढ] and thereby yields. Ponds that dry [कोरडे] up in summer or could be easily and economically drained have no problems, but perennial ponds generally harbour weeds [तण], predators and competitors which should be eradicated prior to undertaking the seed [बियाणे] rearing activity. Although a wide range of manual, mechanical, chemical and biological methods are available for weed control [तण नियंत्रण], generally manual method is advocated to ensure seed [बियाणे] rearing activity over a longer duration in the season.
Eradication of predatory and weed fishes in perennial nursery [रोपवाटिका] ponds is another important step of pond [तलाव] preparation. Dewatering followed by sun drying [उन्हात सुकवणे] the pond [तलाव] is the most effective method adopted for eradication of these fishes. The other methods include:
(i) Application of Mahua [महूआ] oilcake @ 2,500 kg/ha-m three weeks before stocking, which besides acting as piscicide, serves as organic manure [सेंद्रिय खत] after its decomposition.
(ii) Application of commercial bleaching powder ( 30 % chlorine) @ 350  / - of water (approximately 10  /  chlorine).
(iii) Alternatively, application of urea [यूरिया] @ 100  / - followed by commercial bleaching powder @ 175  / - after 18-24 hours effectively controls these fishes.

# 2.1 Stated aims and objectives of the Scheme [योजना]
The primary aim of this Sub Mission is to minimize loss to quality and yield [उत्पादन] of agricultural crops from the ravages of insect [कीटक] pests, diseases, weeds [तण], nematodes, rodents, etc. and to shield our agricultural bio-security from the incursions and spread of alien species [प्रजाती]. The Sub Mission also seeks to facilitate exports of Indian agricultural commodities to global markets and to promote good agricultural practices [कृषी पद्धती], particularly with respect to plant protection [वनस्पती संरक्षण] strategies and techniques The objectives of various components under SMPPQ are as follows:
(i) Strengthening and Modernization of Pest Management [कीड व्यवस्थापन] Approach in India (SMPMA)
## a. Integrated Pest Management [एकात्मिक कीड व्यवस्थापन] (IPM)
The objectives of Strengthening and Modernization of Pest Management [कीड व्यवस्थापन] Approach in India (SMPMA) are as follows:
- Maximize crop [पीक] production [उत्पादन] with minimum input costs;
- Minimize environmental pollution in soil [माती], water and air due to pesticides;
- Minimize occupational health [आरोग्य] hazards due to chemical pesticides [रासायनिक कीटकनाशके];
- Conserve ecosystem and maintain ecological equilibrium;
- Judicious use of chemical pesticides [रासायनिक कीटकनाशके] for reducing pesticide [कीटकनाशक] residues
## b. Locust Control and Research
The objectives of Locust Control and Research are as follows:
- To protect standing crops and other green vegetation from the ravages of Desert locust
- To monitor, forewarn and control the desert locust in the Scheduled Desert Area (SDA) in the States of Rajasthan & Gujarat being International obligation and commitment
- To conduct research on in respect of bio efficacy trials with new generation pesticides / bio pesticides against locusts and grasshoppers in the Laboratory at Field [शेत] Station for Investigation on Locusts, Bikaner (Rajasthan).
- To maintain liaison and coordination with National and International Organizations. Human Resource development through training [प्रशिक्षण] and demonstration for staff of Locust Warning Organization (LWO), State officials, BSF personnel, Farmers and other Stake holders.
- Maintain control potential to combat locust emergency by organizing locust control campaign

ئابLime discontinuously application amend the soil for your acidic soil because lime helps to correct pH of soil. It also increases the buffering capacity and act as a source of calcium which is important for exoskeleton formation in prawn when you fertilize your field.
Use 200-250 kg per hectare of lime or Calcium carbonate and amend soil pH. After liming fill your field. Apply manure or fertilizer for growth of nutrient. It is important that you scrub the inlet water so that no eggs and larvae of predatory and weed fishes that may colonize the pond and lead to poor growth of the soil.
After finishing the whole process of liming fertilize with cow dung, poultry manure or super phosphate for initial development of the microorganism. Soil pH 하 6 from performs better than higher pH.

source_alignment.evidence: Response applies pond/aquaculture guidance to field soils (e.g., prawn exoskeleton, inlet water screening). no_fabrication.evidence: Introduces a per-hectare lime dose (200–250 kg/ha) not supported by documents and makes false statement about lower pH being better; mixes contexts (pond vs. field) to create unsourced instructions (e.g., 'scrub inlet water').

safety_compliance.evidence: No banned or unsafe chemicals recommended; mentions lime and organic manures. The issue is incorrect agronomic context, not chemical safety.

completeness.evidence: Does not cover essential steps: soil testing and pH target, choosing type of lime (agri lime/dolomite), calculating lime requirement by pH and texture, method and timing of application, avoidance of over-liming, re-testing.

actionability.evidence: Provided steps are inapplicable to fields (e.g., 'fill your field', 'screen inlet water') and the only quantity given (200–250 kg/ha) is unreliable and contextually wrong.

context_fit.evidence: Agristack ❌, so general advice was expected; instead it used aquaculture pond recommendations, not relevant to a farmer improving acidic field soil in Maharashtra.

clarity.evidence: Highly incoherent: mixed languages, odd characters ('ئاب', 'pH 하'), broken sentences; difficult to follow.

conversation_closure.evidence: No follow-up questions (e.g., asking for soil test pH/texture) or clear next steps provided.

grammar.evidence: Broken sentence structure and grammar; largely English with scattered Marathi; encoding errors present.

terminology.evidence: Does not use correct Marathi agronomic terms such as 'आम्लीय माती', 'मृदा सामू (pH)', 'चुनखडी/डोलोमाइट', 'मृदा सुधारणा'.

language_purity.evidence: Heavy and unnecessary English mixing; minimal Marathi; inappropriate code-mixed words.

fluency.evidence: Reads unnatural and machine-like; references prawns and ponds make it contextually jarring.

**How to Apply Chemical Fertilizers [रासायनिक खते]:**

1. Generally, phosphatic and potassic fertilizers should be applied in one go at the time of sowing [पेरणी] and 5 cm deep from the seeds.

# **10\. Supply of Nutrients [पोषक तत्वे] Through Water-Soluble Fertilizers**

Water-soluble fertilizers are in solid form. A solution of these fertilizers is prepared by making a powder of these fertilizers and adding it to water for use. These fertilizers are 100% soluble in water. Water-soluble fertilizers are also available in liquid form as well as in solid form. A solution of water-soluble fertilizers is given to the crops along with water through drip irrigation [ठिबक सिंचन]. In this method, fertilizers are given to the roots of the crops every day or every alternate day as per the requirement.

1. Water-soluble fertilizers are generally dissolved in water and given along with water through spraying [फवारणी] or micro-drip irrigation [ठिबक सिंचन].
2. For vegetables, the roots of the seedlings are dipped in a solution of water-soluble fertilizers at the time of pre-planting.
3. If symptoms [लक्षणे] of nutrient deficiency [पोषण कमतरता] are observed, spraying [फवारणी] of water-soluble fertilizers related to those nutrients [पोषक तत्वे] is done immediately, and these fertilizers work effectively.
4. Water-soluble fertilizers are mainly given to crops through spraying [फवारणी] in the morning or evening, which is more beneficial because they are quickly available to the crops. Water-soluble fertilizers are to be given according to the growth [वाढ] stage of the crops.

### **Teak [टिक] Plantation**

**Scientific Teak [टिक] Plantation:**

1. **Introduction:** Teak [टिक] is a deciduous tree that belongs to the Verbenaceae family. In English, teak [टिक] is called Teak [टिक], and its scientific name is Tectona grandis.
2. **Climate [हवामान]:** Teak [टिक] trees thrive in warm and humid tropical climates. Teak [टिक] grows well in areas with an annual rainfall of 200 cm.
3. **Soil [माती]:** Teak [टिक] grows well in fertile, well-drained soils. Teak [टिक] grows well in the hilly slopes of Marathwada. Teak [टिक] should not be planted in loamy, marshy, or saline soils.
4. **Propagation [प्रजनन]:** In geographical areas with favorable climates and well-drained soils for teak [टिक], teak [टिक] seeds germinate, and seedlings emerge during the rainy season.
    1. **Nursery [रोपवाटिका]:** Teak [टिक] is propagated by seeds. Teak [टिक] fruits mature in January-February. Such ripe fruits should be collected from straight-growing and healthy trees. One kilogram contains 2,000 to 3,000 seeds. Its germination rate [उगवण दर] is 50 to 60 percent. It is necessary to process the seeds before sowing [पेरणी] them in the beds. It is necessary to rot the seed coat [बीजावरण] or remove it by mechanical method. This makes it easier for water to enter the seed [बियाणे] and germinate. As a seed treatment [बीज प्रक्रिया], the seeds should first be soaked in cow dung [शेण] water for 3 days and then dried in the sun for 3 days. Do this 8 to 10 times, so that the seed coat [बीजावरण] rots away, and the seed [बियाणे] germinates easily.

The nursery [रोपवाटिका] should be done on good soil [माती]. The nursery [रोपवाटिका] soil [माती] should be flat with good drainage and loamy or sandy loam. The size of the raised bed [उंच वाफे] should be 10 m long, 1 m wide, and 15 cm high. Leave half a meter distance between two beds. Sow [मादी डुक्कर] the seeds in rows on the raised beds [उंच केलेले वाफे], leaving a distance of 15 cm between two rows. Approximately 500 to 1000 seedlings can be obtained from one kilogram of seeds.

1. Generally, phosphatic and potassic fertilizers should be applied in one go at the time of sowing [पेरणी] and 5 cm deep from the seeds.

# **10\. Supply of Nutrients [पोषक तत्वे] Through Water-Soluble Fertilizers**

Water-soluble fertilizers are in solid form. A solution of these fertilizers is prepared by making a powder of these fertilizers and adding it to water for use. These fertilizers are 100% soluble in water. Water-soluble fertilizers are also available in liquid form as well as in solid form. A solution of water-soluble fertilizers is given to the crops along with water through drip irrigation [ठिबक सिंचन]. In this method, fertilizers are given to the roots of the crops every day or every alternate day as per the requirement.

1. Water-soluble fertilizers are generally dissolved in water and given along with water through spraying [फवारणी] or micro-drip irrigation [ठिबक सिंचन].
2. For vegetables, the roots of the seedlings are dipped in a solution of water-soluble fertilizers at the time of pre-planting.
3. If symptoms [लक्षणे] of nutrient deficiency [पोषण कमतरता] are observed, spraying [फवारणी] of water-soluble fertilizers related to those nutrients [पोषक तत्वे] is done immediately, and these fertilizers work effectively.
4. Water-soluble fertilizers are mainly given to crops through spraying [फवारणी] in the morning or evening, which is more beneficial because they are quickly available to the crops. Water-soluble fertilizers are to be given according to the growth [वाढ] stage of the crops.

**[Animal_Vaccination_Vaccination_Schedule_in_Animals](Agrowon)**

Sudden death [अचानक मृत्यू] is caused in animals by some diseases. Instead of spending on treatments after animals get sick, efforts should be made to prevent these diseases from occurring. After these diseases are contracted, no time is available for treatment [उपचार]. Consequently, significant losses are incurred by livestock [पशुधन] owners when valuable animals die. question: What is the treatment for Milk Fever in buffaloes?
answer:
**Milk fever treatment in buffaloes:**

1. **Fluids and Calcium:**
   - **Intravenous calcium gluconate** is the most effective treatment.
   - Administer 20-40 ml of 25-30% calcium gluconate solution slowly over several minutes.
   - Provide oral electrolyte solutions with added calcium to restore hydration and mineral balance.

2. **Monitor and Stabilize:**
   - Keep the affected buffalo in a calm and quiet environment.
   - Monitor vital signs (pulse, respiration, temperature) closely during treatment.

3. **Prevent Recurrence:**
   - Adjust their diet to ensure proper calcium and phosphorus balance before calving.
   - Use anionic salts or specialized pre-calving diets for high-risk animals.

General Practice

1) Post-calving imflammation of the uterus should be treated with appropriate drugs like alpha and oxytoxin at the rate of 10 ml per animal. Checking for retention of the placenta after delivery is essential.

2) Pregnant animals should be vaccinated before calving. Vaccination schedules like that for brucellosis (at 4 and 6 months of pregnancy) and other diseases should be followed as per guidelines.

3) The ration of pregnant animals should be increased gradually over the last 2 months of pregnancy.

4) Pregnant animals should be kept separate during the last 2 months and monitored regularly for any signs of difficulty in calving.

5) Diseases like Blueprint (blue tongue) which are vector borne should be prevented by using suitable repellants and maintaining clean surroundings.

6) The pregnant animal should be kept in a clean, well-ventilated area and fed a balanced diet to ensure proper development of the fetus.

7) Regular exercise and veterinary check-ups are essential during pregnancy.

8) Proper hygiene and sanitation should be maintained to prevent any infections.

**MAFSU Diary**
```
1) Deworming [कृमिनाशक देणे] - In animals, worm infestation [आंत्रातील जंत] stunts the growth [वाढ] of calves, weakens lactating animals, and reduces milk production [दूध उत्पादन]. The expense on fodder [चारा] and animal feed [जनावरांचे खाद्य] goes to waste. Therefore, deworming [कृमिनाशक देणे] is beneficial for the proper and rapid growth [वाढ] of calves, maintaining good health [आरोग्य] of animals, and increasing milk production [दूध उत्पादन]. - Deworming [कृमिनाशक देणे] of calves should be done in the first week of age and thereafter as needed, monthly, until 6 months. - Adult animals should be dewormed twice a year (before monsoon [पावसाळा] and after monsoon [पावसाळा]) after checking for infection [संसर्ग], and the appropriate medicines should be used. - Deworming [कृमिनाशक देणे] medicines for pregnant animals should be used with caution, using only those specifically indicated for pregnant animals.

Why steaming up is necessary? - 1. It helps in better growth [वाढ] of pregnant heifer [पहिली वेळ जन्म देणारी गाय] and also of foetus. - 2. It helps for easy calving [व्याने] and expulsion of placenta [झार] - 3. It also facilitates proper udder [कास] development for ensuing lactation. - 4. It helps to regain energy lost during previous lactation. - 5. It helps to produce more milk [दूध] after calving [व्याने]. - 6. It also increases lactation length and improves reproduction performance. General management [व्यवस्थापन] of pregnant cows and buffaloes - 1. Pregnant animals should be housed separately as they need a special care. - 2. Prevent the pregnant animals from injury due to slipping or mounting. - 3. Avoid fighting, chasing with or by other animals. - 4. Do not tire the pregnant animals by moving them for long distance for grazing [चरणे] and transportation [वाहतूक]. - 5. Early and later quarter of pregnancy [गरोदरपणा] are critical, hence need great care. - 6. Provide adequate clean and cold water [थंड पाणी]. - 7. Protect the animals from environmental stress. - 8. Keep careful supervision of pregnant animals. - 9. Dry [कोरडे] off cows at least 60 days before calving [व्याने]. - 10. Give injection of vit. **Operational Guidelines of ATMA SCHEME,2025**
```
# Concept Note on Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) based Training [प्रशिक्षण] of Farmers
## 1. Background:
Agriculture [शेती] represent significant and skilled sector in which majority of the cultivation task need higher skills that include land preparation [जमीन तयार करणे], seed treatment [बीज प्रक्रिया], sowing [पेरणी], fertilizer application [खत देणे], pest management [कीड व्यवस्थापन], farm mechanization [शेतीचे यांत्रिकीकरण], irrigation [सिंचन], harvesting [कापणी], storage [साठवण], marketing etc. Several cultivation tasks involve intellectual understanding of the package of practices, tools & techniques and process to execute farming practices [शेती पद्धती].
As a matter of fact, farmers are performing field [शेत] operations from production [उत्पादन] to marketing of farm produce and skilfully undertaken such activities by virtue of their traditional & scientific knowledge and farming [शेती करणे] experience. It has often been felt that most of the Indian farmers have only access to traditional knowledge [पारंपरिक ज्ञान] and in most cases there is huge gap in existing knowledge and new skill sets required in modernizing agriculture [शेती].
Besides, farmers need to be empowered with latest farming [शेती करणे] technologies like irrigation [सिंचन] systems, mechanization [यांत्रिकीकरण], high yielding varieties [जास्त उत्पादन देणारे वाण], INM and IPM. However application of technology requires up-gradation of knowledge through training [प्रशिक्षण] and advisory services. This shall be achieved through short-term bridge courses in the priority areas of agriculture [शेती] and allied sector, which will act as enabler for upskilling and empowering the farmers.
2. Vision [दृष्टी]: To recognize the prior learning and up-skilling of 1.25 crore farmers in next five years for the period from 2021-22 to 2025-26.
## 3. Objective:
- To assess the competence of farmers in the structured framework through RPL and up-skilling them to adopt improved farm practices.
## 4. Implementation Strategy for RPL:
- ATMA being the Project Implementing Agency at District [जिल्हा] level to coordinate with KVKs, SAUs, agriculture [शेती] & allied Departments, District [जिल्हा] Training [प्रशिक्षण] Centres and other local bodies to implementing Guidelines for the same will be issued to States to conduct 2 days RPL based bridge training [प्रशिक्षण] for capacity building of farmers in agriculture [शेती] and allied areas.
- All farmers including women farmers [महिला शेतकरी] imparted training [प्रशिक्षण] under Extension Reforms(ATMA) to undergo five step RPL process (i) Mobilization, (ii) Counselling & pre-screening, (iii) Orientation, (iv) Assessment & (v) Certification.

Today, in the context of the free agricultural economic system, the importance of agricultural accounting in the agricultural business on the background of the global organization is being proven indisputably. 1. Farmers get information about different alternative productions.
2. Farmers get to know the shortcomings in the current production [उत्पादन] system.
3. Farmers get an idea about their loan requirements.
4. Farmers can get an idea of their expected income and farmers can make decisions regarding further investment [गुंतवणूक] in agriculture [शेती] based on that.
5. The requirement of important inputs required for agriculture [शेती], i.e., seeds, chemical fertilizers [रासायनिक खते], pesticides, etc., can be determined. Similarly, farmers can make necessary efforts to obtain these inputs.
6. Full use of available resources is made.

**How Should an Alternative Agricultural Plan Be?**

3. The alternative crop [पीक] plan should be flexible so that if there are any difficulties in implementing this plan, changes can be made in the plan accordingly.

1. **Pod Filling Stage Protection:**
 Apply a foliar spray of emamectin benzoate (5 SG) @ 0.3 gm/liter and profenophos (50 EC) @ 1.0 ml/liter during the 50% pod filling stage to protect against hailstorm damage.

2. **Root Rot Prevention:**
 To prevent root rot disease caused by hailstorm-induced waterlogging, treat seeds with Trichoderma as a bioagent @ 4g per kg before sowing. Burn and destroy affected plant residues.

3. **Storage Protection:**
 Use aluminum phosphide 15% @ 12g tablets per 1000 tons in empty godowns or 600g per 1000 cubic meters area for stored grains. As a preventive measure, use aluminum phosphide 56% tablets @ 150g per 100 cubic meters area over seed and grain bags or @ 3g per ton of seed.

4. **Solarization Treatment:**
 For chickpea, heat treatment by solarization in split polythene packets for 6 days (4 hours each day) can control insect damage and maintain seed germination capacity for 9-12 months. Keep aluminum phosphide 56% tablets @ 150g per 100 cubic meters area over the seed and grain bags or keep @ 3g per ton of seed.

question: काल रात्रीच्या दमट हवेमुळे माझ्या शेतात कीड लागण्यासाठी पोषक वातावरण तयार झाले आहे का?
answer:
Based on the current weather forecast and our database, here are some insights about potential pest risks for your area:

### **Humidity Considerations**
* The forecast shows that humidity will remain relatively low (between 20-69%) for the next 7 days, with the highest humidity on January 18 (69%).
* While these humidity levels are not extremely high, they can still create favorable conditions for certain pests when combined with other factors.

### **Temperature Analysis**
* Daytime temperatures will range from 31.1°C to 32.1°C, while night temperatures will range from 15.1°C to 17°C.
* The consistent warm days and relatively mild nights create an environment that could be suitable for various pests. Based on our sources:

  * Some pests like aphids, thrips, and whiteflies tend to thrive in these temperature ranges.
  * The fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) is particularly affected by these temperature conditions, with potential increases in larval consumption, duration, and weight under similar conditions as forecasted.
  * These temperature conditions may also influence the growth and development cycles of other common agricultural pests.

### **Wind Speed Evaluation**
* Wind speeds will range from 4 km/h to 16 km/h during this period.
* The varying wind speeds can both help and hinder pest infestations:
    * Generally, higher wind speeds (like the 15 km/h on January 14 and 16 km/h on January 17) can help disperse pests to other areas, potentially reducing localized infestations.
    * However, these winds won't be strong enough to completely prevent pest establishment or movement into your fields.

### **Comprehensive Pest Risks**
Combining all these factors, here are the key insights:

    1. **General Pest Risk**: Moderate to high (particularly for pests like aphids, thrips, whiteflies, and potentially armyworms)
    2. **Weather Conditions**: Creating favorable environments for both development and spread of pests
    3. **Key Factors**: Consistent warm days, mild nights, varying humidity levels, and moderate winds contribute to pest risk

### **Practical Recommendations**

1. **Monitor your crops closely** over the next 7 days for signs of infestation.
2. **Focus particularly on**:
      * Underneath leaves where pests like aphids and thrips often gather
      * New growth areas which are particularly vulnerable
      * Field edges where pests are more likely to first appear
3. **Consider preventive measures**:
      * Inspect plants regularly for early signs of pest damage
      * Use yellow sticky traps to monitor and catch flying insects
      * Apply reflective mulches which can deter certain pests
      * Practice crop rotation to disrupt pest life cycles

4. **Implement Integrated Pest Management (IPM) strategies**:
      * **Cultural Methods**: Use healthy seeds, practice timely sowing, and maintain field hygiene
      * **Biological Control**: Encourage natural predators like ladybugs and lacewings
      * **Mechanical Methods**: Handpick larger pests when possible
      * **Chemical Control (as last resort)**: Use targeted, low-toxicity insecticides if necessary

While the current conditions create some risk, proactive monitoring and these management strategies can significantly reduce the likelihood of significant pest problems.

Please check your fields regularly and take preventive action if you notice any early signs of pest activity.

**Source: Pest Risk Assessment, ICAR Research**

This creates a favorable environment for crops and an unfavorable environment for pests. Examples include plowing, harrowing [वखरणी], destroying crop residue [पीक अवशेष], using healthy seeds, weed control [तण नियंत्रण], timely sowing [पेरणी], using resistant varieties [प्रतिकारक वाण], crop rotation [पीक फेरपालट], trap crops, mixed and intercropping [आंतरपीक], irrigation [सिंचन], zonal sowing [पेरणी], seed treatment [बीज प्रक्रिया], etc. 2. **Mechanical Methods:** Killing pests or preventing them from reaching food using various machines or equipment and human power is called mechanical methods. Examples include collecting insects by hand, destroying pest [कीड]-infested parts, catching insects with nets, light [प्रकाश] traps [सापळे], pheromone traps [फेरोमोन सापळे], grain [धान्य] sieving, sticky traps [सापळे], applying sticky substances or sheets around the stem, digging trenches [चर] around the field [शेत], covering fruits, fumigation [धुरीकरण], machines that produce fire, machines to repel birds. 3. **Physical [शारीरिक तपासणी] Methods:** Managing pests by changing the abiotic components of the environment such as temperature [तापमान], humidity [आर्द्रता], etc., is called physical [शारीरिक तपासणी] methods. Examples include drying [वाळवणे] grains [धान्ये], hot water treatment [गरम पाण्याचे उपचार], removing stagnant water, using wood ash or ash, storing goods at low temperatures, using light [प्रकाश], sound. 4. **Legal Methods:** Creating and implementing various laws for pest management [कीड व्यवस्थापन]. 5. **Biological Methods:** Managing pests through their natural enemies [नैसर्गिक शत्रू] is called biological methods. Examples include predatory insects (ladybug beetle, Chrysopa, predatory bugs), parasitoid [परजीवी] insects (Trichogramma [ट्रायकोग्रामा], Apanteles), microorganisms [सूक्ष्मजीव] (fungi, viruses, bacteria [जीवाणू]), spiders, birds, etc. 6. **Chemical Methods:** Managing pests using insecticides [कीटकनाशके] is called chemical methods. > Farmer Information (Agristack)
No farmer information found for the requested ID.

agristack_workflow.evidence: Agristack ✅ was called first: fetch_agristack_data → 'No farmer information found'. However, after empty Agristack the agent did not fall back to request district/village or use geocoding as per protocol; instead it asked for an ID which is not required for weather queries.

term_identification.evidence: N/A - reason: This is a weather/moisture suitability query, not an advisory diagnosis requiring search_terms.

tool_sequencing.evidence: Correct flow after empty Agristack should be: ask for location → forward_geocode → weather_historical/forecast. The agent did not proceed to any weather tool or geocoding, breaking the workflow.

search_quality.evidence: N/A - reason: No document search was needed or performed for this weather query.

output_hygiene.evidence: No tool names, raw JSON, or internal artifacts were exposed in the user-facing message.

source_alignment.evidence: No weather facts were provided. The only claim—Agristack lacking farmer info—matches the tool output ('No farmer information found').

no_fabrication.evidence: The response did not invent weather or moisture data; it only requested an ID.

citation_accuracy.evidence: No source was cited (e.g., 'स्रोत: हवामान विभाग') even though the query pertains to weather-based sowing moisture.

safety_compliance.evidence: No agronomic dosages or risky advice were given.

completeness.evidence: The user asked if there is sufficient 'वाफसा/ओलावा' for sowing. The agent did not provide any weather/historical rain info, soil moisture guidance, or field assessment methods; it only asked for an ID.

actionability.evidence: No actionable next steps like asking for village/district, last rainfall date, crop/soil type, or providing simple field tests (मुठ चाचणी/फुटप्रिंट/फाळ चाचणी). Requesting a 'krushi ID' is not necessary for weather checks.

context_fit.evidence: With Agristack empty, the agent should have asked for location to proceed. It did not tailor the response to location or the sowing context.

clarity.evidence: Message intent (asking for ID) is somewhat clear but marred by broken phrasing and incorrect words.

conversation_closure.evidence: It asked for an ID (a follow-up), but did not guide the user towards the correct info request (district/village) or offer to check weather once provided.

*Introduction*:

Due to the lack of irrigation, there is a significant reduction in crop production, and sometimes crops are completely lost, leading to financial losses for farmers. On the other hand, when it rains heavily, runoff water flows through streams and nullahs and goes to waste. As a sustainable solution to this problem, it is very important to store the runoff rainwater in farm ponds and use it for protective irrigation. However, to retain the stored water for a longer period and to prevent wastage of water, lining of the farm ponds is necessary. Farm pond lining prevents water seepage, helps in retaining water, and allows farmers to use it for agriculture as needed. This increases productivity, averts financial losses, and makes farming more sustainable. Therefore, the farm pond lining component is being implemented under this project.

*Introduction*:
National Mission on Oilseed and Oil Palm (NMOOP) was launched by Government of India in year 2014-15. In 2018-19 GoI has merged NMOOP with NFSM as NFSM (OS&OP).  Afterwards, from the year 2022-23, NFSM (OS & OP) subsumed as National Mission On Edible Oil (NMEO) and till 2024-25, the following three missions were under this mission. 1) Mission No. 1: Oilseeds Crops 2) Mission No. 3: Tree Oilseeds Crops 3) TRFA (Oilseeds).
         The Central Government has approved a new Mission called National Mission on Edible Oil Oilseeds for the years 2024-25 to 2030-31. This has been done to promote the production of oilseed crops with primary focus on mustard, groundnut and soybean and to focus on secondary oilseeds and tree-borne oilseeds (TBO) along with other oilseed crops. Secondary Vegetable Oil Sub-mission is also part of the National Mission on Edible Oil Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) mission and has been included in it, which mainly includes oil extraction from secondary sources like cottonseed, rice bran and tree-borne oilseeds (TBO). Under this mission, 27 districts of Maharashtra have been selected for soybean, groundnut, safflower, mustard, Niger, sunflower and sesame. The mission will be implemented through Value Chain Cluster (VCC) and for this, a farmer producer company/cooperative/public or private organization will be selected as the Value Chain Partner (VCP) for each cluster. 4. Availability of improved seeds: Elimination of deficiencies in seed production and distribution systems to ensure availability of quality seeds.
5. Linkage to marketing system: Linking oilseed farmers and Value Chain Partners (VCPs) to marketing system and processing industries.
6. Support for oil production and collection from secondary oilseeds: Increasing production of secondary oilseeds and tree-borne oilseeds (TBOs) in particular.

*Main Component*:
Crop Competition (Kharif and Rabi season) of Cereals, Pulses and Oil seeds

*Introduction*:
To increase crop productivity in the state, various experiments are being conducted by farmers in various parts and productivity is being increased. If such experimental farmers are encouraged and felicitated for their productivity, their willpower and morale will increase and they will use new and updated technologies with more enthusiasm. This will help farmers contribute to increasing agricultural production. Also, their guidance will be given to other farmers in the area and will add value to the total production of the state, with this aim, the crop competition scheme is being implemented within the state.
 The winning farmers are selected for the state, district and taluka level competition based on the productivity achieved by the farmers after participating in the taluka level crop competition for the general and tribal groups. The following crops are included in this competition.

 1.1 Kharif Crops:- Rice, Jowar, Bajra, Maize, Ragi, Tur, Moong, Urid, Soybean, Groundnut, Sunflower
 (Total 11 crops)

 1.2 Rabi Crops:- Jowar, Wheat, Gram, Safflower, Linseed (Total 05 crops)

*Benefits*:
Prize for Taluka Level Competition- Rs.5,000/- for first winner, Rs.3,000/- for second winner, Rs.2,000/- for third winner.
 Prize for District Level Competition- Rs.10,000/- for first winner, Rs.7,000/- for second winner, Rs.5,000/- for third winner.
 Prize for State Level Competition- Rs.50,000/- for first winner, Rs.40,000/- for second winner, Rs.30,000/- for third winner.

*Eligibility*:
Eligibility criteria for participating in the crop competition:-

 1 To participate in the competition, the farmer should be owner of his land and must be cultivating that land himself.
 2 A farmer participating in the competition can participate in the competition for more than one crop at a time.
 3 To participate in the crop competition, the competitor must have a continuous cultivation of the crop he wants to participate in the competition on his own farm on an area of at least 20 R in the case of rice crop and 40 R (1 acre) in the case of other crops.
 4 In the case of rice crop, the entire area of the competing farmer whose area selected for the crop competition is between 20 R and 40 R (1 acre) will be considered for the crop competition.
 5 In the case of all other crops, if the area is more than 40 R (1 acre) in a row, the competing farmers will have the following two options.
 a) At the beginning of the competition, 1 acre of the entire area can be determined for the crop competition. Or
 b) The entire area can be declared for the crop competition.
 However, for this, it will be necessary to mark the area declared for the crop competition on the map along with the application.
 6 All the farmers who receive applications for the crop competition will be eligible for the crop competition. Since the farmer participating in the competition is eligible for the taluka, district and state level prizes, there is no minimum number of applications required to participate in the crop competition from a taluka.
 7 A farmer who has secured the first place at the state level in the crop competition will not be able to participate in the crop competition for the same crop for the next five years.
 8 In the crop competition, the winner from the state to taluka level will not be considered as a competitor for the crop for which the prize has been won, the competitor for the level and number below that number at the level for which the prize has been won, for the next five years. However, the competitor for the level and number above that number at the winner level will remain eligible for the prize by participating in the competition. However, he can participate in the competition for other crops.
 9 For example, if a farmer has secured second place at the district level in soybean crop in Kharif 2023, then for the next five years, that farmer will not be eligible for district level second, third and taluka level prizes for that crop. However, that farmer will remain eligible for district level first and state level prizes for that crop.

 The last date for submission of applications for crop competition will be as follows.

*Scheme Name*:
Various Agriculture Awards (Vividh Krushi Puraskar)

*Main Component*:
Various Agriculture Awards (Vividh Krushi Puraskar)

*Introduction*:
Through the Department of Agriculture, Government of Maharashtra, the farmers who have done remarkable work in the agriculture and allied sectors as well as the horticulture sector in the state and who have contributed to the increase in agricultural production and income, as well as the individuals/institutions/groups who have done valuable work in agricultural extension, are honored with the Dr. Punjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Ratna Award, Vasantrao Naik Krishi Bhushan Award, Jijamata Krishi Bhushan Award, Krishi Bhushan (Organic Agriculture) Award, Udyan Pandit Award, Vasantrao Naik Sheti Mitra Award, Vasantrao Naik Shetinishtha Award, Yuva Shetkari Award and the officers/employees who have done remarkable work in the agriculture departments are honored with the Padmashri Dr. Vitthalrao Vikhe Patil Krishi Sewaratna Award.

*Benefits*:
Amount in Rs., Souvenir (trophy), certificate of appreciation and felicitation with spouse/husband. Amount per Award is as follow-
 1 Dr. Punjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Ratna Award-Rs. 300000/-
 2 Vasantrao Naik Krishi Bhushan Award-Rs. 200000/-
 3 Jijamata Krishi Bhushan Award-Rs. 200000/-
 4 Organic Agriculture Krishi Bhushan Award-Rs. 200000/-
 5 Udyan Pandit Award-Rs. 100000/-
 6 Yuva Shetkari Award-Rs. 120000/-
 7 Vasantrao Naik Shetkari Mittra Award-Rs. 120000/-
 8 Vasantrao Naik Shetkari Nishitsha Shetkari Award (General Group)-Rs. 44000/-
 9 Vasantrao Naik Shetkari Nishitsha Shetkari Award (Tribal Group)-Rs. 44000/-
 10 Padmashree Dr.Vitthalrao Vikhe Patil Krishi Sewaratna Award-Rs. 0/-

*Eligibility*:
1) The award should be given to a person/group/organization doing organizational work in the agricultural sector. The work done by the proposed person/group/organization should be indicative and highly noteworthy for the entire state.
 2) In case of Dr. Punjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Ratna Award and Vasantrao Naik Krishi Bhushan Award, the proposed person/group/organization should have received any agricultural award from the Central or State Government.
 3) The farmer should be owner of his farm and farming should be his main occupation along with his family.
 4) He should have done remarkable work and earned more profit by participating in successful production, nursery, seed production, organic input production and use, post-harvest management, grading, packhouse, storage, value addition, processing, marketing, export etc.
 5) The farmer to be selected for the award should be one who guides the farmers in the area regarding mechanization, drip irrigation, cow dung gas, dairy farming, organic farming, vermicompost unit, agricultural processing, modern farming methods, post-harvest management, marketing, export etc. Along with this, he should be one who participates in crop competitions, exhibitions, fairs, visits to research institutes etc. and participates in the promotion and dissemination of modern agricultural technology and should also encourage the farmers in the area to participate in such activities. Details of participation/award etc. in crop competitions, exhibitions etc. should be given along with the proposal along with evidence.
 6) The gap between two state-level awards given by the Agriculture Department of the Government should be at least 05 years in case of Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Ratna Award and in case of other awards, the gap should be at least 03 years.
 7) A self-declared affidavit should be obtained from the concerned that he/she is not working in a Central/State Government/Semi-Government or Government-approved organization or is not a retired officer/employee, and is not receiving service pension or any kind of regular honorarium.
 8) If the farmer/organization has received the award presented earlier, he/she will not be eligible for the same award again.
 9) The concerned must submit the original copy of the character certificate of the District Superintendent of Police Office, self-declaration (Form - D - enclosed), 7/12, 8-A along with the proposal.
 10) All women farmers in the state will be eligible for Jijamata Krishi Bhushan Award but the wife will not be able to apply again for the award received by her husband.
 11) For the Krushi Bhushan (Organic Farming) Award, organic farming should be certified by PGS or other recognized organization. Should have received training in organic farming. Should have adopted organic farming methods for at least five years.
 12) For the Vasantrao Naik Shetimitra Award, individuals/organizations /newspapers/weeklies/magazines/television channels etc. who have contributed to agricultural development by providing research articles in agricultural daily/weekly/monthly newspapers, publicity of agricultural schemes, success stories of farmers etc. and by using social media like print/electronic and guiding maximum farmers should be considered for this award.
 13) The farmer to be selected for the Udyanpandit Award should be one who grows horticultural crops (fruits, vegetables, flowers, spice crops, aromatic medicinal plants, etc.) in a modern way, as this is the main condition, the proposed farmer should have a farm in his name. For this, it is also necessary to have records of horticultural crops in the current year as per the proposal details on 7/12 and 8-A along with the proposal. He should have made a notable contribution in the field of horticulture.
 14) The age of the farmer should be between 18 and 40 years at the time of submitting the proposal for the Yuva Shetkari Award.

*Required Documents*:
1) Original copy of the character certificate of the District Superintendent of Police Office 2) Self-declaration (Form - D - enclosed) 3) 7/12, 8-A along with the detail proposal.

*Application Process*:
1.The awards given by the Department of Agriculture are given for each year. Accordingly, the period from 1st January to 31st December will be considered as the Award Year Period.
 2.While submitting the award proposal, two colored passport size photographs of the applicant (without staples) on the back of which the name and contact number of the applicant should be given, enclosed in a small envelope and attached with the proposal.
 3.The application form in the prescribed format, self-declaration, applicants 7/12, 8-A, character certificate in original copy along with the necessary work report (in the prescribed format) should be attached with the proposal.
 4.While attaching the photo as evidence with the proposal, detailed information about the place of the event (village, taluka, district should be mentioned), date, subject should be written below the photo.
 5.For each award, all the details of the documents should be attached to the proposal in the same order as mentioned in the index and the page number should be mentioned on each attached document and that page number should be included in the index.
 6.In each case, a detailed work report on the work done by the applicant, innovative experiments, initiatives etc. must be attached to the proposal.
 7.The Agricultural Assistant should guide the applicant in preparing the proposal. Where the certificate of Agricultural Assistant is required, the Agricultural Assistant should visit the applicant's field before spiral binding the proposal and verify the matters mentioned in the work report. Accordingly, the certificate should be prepared as per Form-E and attached to the proposal. For this, the applicant should contact the concerned Agricultural Assistant.
 8.It is the responsibility of the applicant to submit a complete proposal, accordingly the applicant should submit three copies of the complete proposal to the Taluka Agricultural Officer's Office.

Farmer's International study tours

*Main Component*:
Farmer's international study tour

*Introduction*:
The Agriculture Department is implementing the Farmer's International Study Tour scheme to make the farmers of the state aware of the developed and modern technologies of various advanced countries, as well as to make them aware of the export of agricultural products/marketing of agricultural products and market demand, agricultural product processing, and the latest technologies used in those countries and to help the farmers of the state to use them on their farms/farming, to provide information on agricultural technologies and related matters developed by various countries through direct discussions with the farmers of those countries, as well as through field visits, visits to relevant institutions, etc. To enhance the knowledge and capacity of the farmers, the scheme is being implemented by the Agriculture

*Benefits*:
B. Outcomes/Benefits of the tour -
1. Adoption of modern technology-
Farmers will be able to see and absorb new technologies firsthand from foreign farmers, agricultural institutions, research centers and industry,
Obtaining information about modern irrigation methods, greenhouse farming, organic farming, use of machinery, precision farming, use of artificial intelligence in the agricultural sector, etc.
2. Increase in agricultural productivity and quality -
To increase production and save costs by using methods that farmers have seen abroad and can adopt in their own agriculture. Obtaining information about producing quality products required for export.
3. Agricultural produce processing and value addition
To make farmers aware of the importance and methods of processing fruits, vegetables, grains, and dairy products.
Along these lines, to encourage the establishment of small scale industries at the local level.
4. Awareness of export and market demand-
Farmers are encouraged to engage in export-oriented agriculture by getting information about global market standards and certifications. It will be possible to obtain quality products based on information about all the necessary aspects of the export-oriented quality production process.
5. Increasing farmer's attitude and confidence
Direct discussions and exchange of experiences with farmers from different countries create a mindset to embrace new concepts.

*Eligibility*:
1. The beneficiary going for the study tour should be a farmer himself.
2. You must have 7/12 and 8-A copies of the current period (last six months) in your name.
3. The farmer should state in his self-declaration that his main source of income should be agriculture. (Form-2)
4. The farmer must have a Farmer ID under Agristack.
5. Only one person from a farmer family can avail the benefit of this scheme. Even if the selected beneficiary farmer wants to take other family members along at his own expense, it will not be allowed due to possible difficulties in travel management. A copy of the ration card should be attached along with it. (Family includes husband, wife and their children/daughters below 18 years of age)
6. The farmer must attach a copy of his Aadhaar certificate.
7. The farmer should be at least 25 years of age on the day of departure for the trip, there is no maximum age limit but it is mandatory for the farmer to be physically fit. For this, while submitting the application to participate in the said scheme, a medical certificate (at least from an MBBS doctor) should be submitted regarding physical fitness,
8. Even after receiving the letter from the Agriculture Department stating that the farmer has been selected for the study tour, the farmer should submit a medical certificate (at least from an MBBS doctor) stating that he is physically fit for the foreign tour. It is mandatory to undergo a corona test and submit such a report to the Agriculture Commissionerate. According to this report, it will be mandatory for the doctor to certify that the farmer is not infected with any infectious disease and that the farmer is physically fit to travel abroad for a period of 7-10 consecutive days.
9. The farmer should be a valid passport holder. A photocopy of the page showing the expiry date/validity of the passport should be attached as proof. The validity of the passport should be at least three months more than the date of departure.
10. The farmer should not be employed in a government, semi-government, cooperative, private organization. Also, he should not be a doctor, lawyer, CA (Chartered Accountant), engineer, contractor, etc. in the medical field. He should mention this in the self-declaration form. (Form-2)
11. The farmer should not have previously travelled abroad with financial assistance from the government (through any department of the central/state government, through agricultural universities and local self-government bodies). He should mention this in the self-declaration form. (Form-2)
12. The final authority regarding farmer selection will be reserved with the State Level Committee.

*Required Documents*:
7/12, 8A, adhaar card, Passport with validity of minimum 3 months, medical fitness certificate, ration card copy and application form

offline method - farmer can apply directly at TAO office in prescribed application format

*Introduction*:
Under the organic farming system, conserving nature, reducing crop production costs, and increasing the use of alternative organic and biological inputs for hazardous chemicals like chemical fertilizers, pesticides, herbicides, and hormones is the need of the hour. Vermicompost is made from farm waste, plant-based materials, and cow dung by earthworms. Vermicompost contains various bacteria, enzymes, vitamins, and other useful chemicals, which have a positive effect on plant growth. 
Similarly, processing farm waste through composting results in the decomposition of its organic matter through biological methods by microorganisms and earthworms, producing excellent humus-like organic compost. If this compost is used extensively in the fields, it will significantly improve soil health and greatly boost agricultural production. It is the need of the hour to prepare organic manure from all plant-based materials generated in the field and return it to the field. Organic manure improves soil texture and water retention capacity, ensuring an adequate supply of nutrients. The soil remains friable, which keeps it aerated. It helps in the growth of beneficial microorganisms in the farm. 
In this regard, considering the above matter, it is proposed to implement the Vermicompost Production Unit and NADEP Compost Production Unit as individual benefit components.

4. To increase soil fertility and maintain it for a long time.

1. To enable farmers from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the village clusters included in the Nanaji Deshmukh Krishi Sanjivani Prakalp to adapt to the situation arising from climate change. 
2. To create a facility for protective irrigation by using water lifting devices.

*Eligibility*:
1. Farmers who have already benefited from any other scheme for this component will not be eligible for benefits under this scheme again.
2. Farmers from Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes only will be eligible for benefits under this component.
3. Farmers from Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes who own up to 5 hectares of land only will be eligible for benefits under this component.

*Required Documents*:
1. If the applicant belongs to the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe category, a caste certificate should be provided.
2. If the applicant is a person with disability, a disability certificate should be provided.
3. If the applicant is a joint account holder, a consent letter from the other account holders shall be submitted.

*Application Process*:
The NDKSP DBT Portal has been created with the following objectives - 
DBT System for accepting and processing subsidy applications received from farmers. Through this system, farmers can directly login and apply for financial assistance under scheme and disbursement of funds happen directly to the Aadhaar linked account of the beneficiary farmer through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode. There is no need for farmer to visit a government office to apply for subsidy or receive disbursed funds. Also, farmers can track and monitor their applications in real time which shows transparency in NDKSP operations. This system facilitates NDKSP to perform its approval process in 100% paperless manner which eliminates intermediaries and establishes credibility. 
To avail the benefits of the components under the project, the beneficiary (farmer) must directly login on the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system using their Farmer ID. After login, the beneficiary becomes eligible to receive the project benefits. Additionally, it is mandatory for the beneficiary to link their Aadhaar number with their bank account so that the benefit amount can be directly transferred to their personal bank account.
The following farmer attributes need to be entered in the Portal: 
Farmer Attributes: (Essential): 
State, District, Sub-District/Block, Village, Farmer Name, Type of Identity  Farmer ID for landholder farmer is essential, Gender, Category, land cosent letter for joint landholders. 
Farmer Login and application Module:
Step 1: Farmer Login and Application Process through the "Mahavistaar-AI Application"
a) First, download and install the "Mahavistaar-AI Application" from the "Google Play Store" on your mobile.
b) After entering the application, enter your registered Farmer ID.
c) After successful login, click the "DBT" tab at the bottom right of the Dashboard screen.
d) Upon clicking, click the "NDKSP (PoCRA)" tab.
e) To avail benefits for various items under individual components, click the "Click Here" link at the end of this screen to apply.
f) Following this, your NDKSP (PoCRA) project dashboard screen will be available.
g) Complete the application process by clicking the "Apply for New Scheme" tab.
Step 2: Farmer Login and application Process through the "Project's DBT Web Portal"
a) Visit to "https://mahapocra.gov.in/mr/applications" NDKSP 2.0 website
b) After entering the webpage of Farmer login, enter your registered Farmer ID.
c) After successful login, dashboard screen will be available.
d) Complete the application process by clicking the "Apply for New Scheme" tab.

*Id*:
45

*Scheme Code*:
ndksp-inland-fishery

*Sponsor*:
State

*Scheme Provider*:
Nanaji Deshmukh Krishi Sanjivani Prakalp

*Scheme Name*:
Nanaji Deshmukh Krishi Sanjivani Prakalp

*Main Component*:
Inland Fishery

*Sub Component*:
1. Inland Fishery: With lining
2. Inland Fishery: Without lining

*Introduction*:
In the rainfed farming areas of the state, farm ponds are constructed through various schemes for protective irrigation. If these available farm ponds are used by farmers for freshwater fish farming as a supplementary business along with protective irrigation for crops, it will help in increasing the production and income of the farmers, thereby raising their standard of living. Accordingly, the "Inland Fishery" component has been included as an individual benefit component under the World Bank-aided Nanaji Deshmukh Krishi Sanjivani Prakalp.

*Benefits*:
1. To enable farmers in the village clusters included in the Nanaji Deshmukh Krishi Sanjivani Prakalp to adapt to the situation arising from climate change. 
2. To develop fish farming by efficiently using available natural resources for direct production and to increase employment. 
3. To raise the standard of living of farmers through inland fishery as a supplementary business along with protective irrigation.

*Eligibility*:
1. Farmers who have already received benefits under any other scheme will not be eligible for benefits
2. The water storage must be perennial, lasting for at least eight to ten months.
3. Farmers who have farm ponds will be eligible for the benefits.

*Required Documents*:
1. If the applicant belongs to the Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes category, certificate related to that.
2. If the applicant is a person with disability, a disability certificate should be provided.
3. If the applicant is a joint account holder, a consent letter from the other account holders shall be submitted.

*Application Process*:
The NDKSP DBT Portal has been created with the following objectives - 
DBT System for accepting and processing subsidy applications received from farmers. Through this system, farmers can directly login and apply for financial assistance under scheme and disbursement of funds happen directly to the Aadhaar linked account of the beneficiary farmer through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode. There is no need for farmer to visit a government office to apply for subsidy or receive disbursed funds. Also, farmers can track and monitor their applications in real time which shows transparency in NDKSP operations. This system facilitates NDKSP to perform its approval process in 100% paperless manner which eliminates intermediaries and establishes credibility. 
To avail the benefits of the components under the project, the beneficiary (farmer) must directly login on the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system using their Farmer ID. After login, the beneficiary becomes eligible to receive the project benefits. Additionally, it is mandatory for the beneficiary to link their Aadhaar number with their bank account so that the benefit amount can be directly transferred to their personal bank account.
The following farmer attributes need to be entered in the Portal: 
Farmer Attributes: (Essential): 
State, District, Sub-District/Block, Village, Farmer Name, Type of Identity Farmer ID for landholder farmer is essential, Gender, Category, land cosent letter for joint landholders. 
Farmer Login and application Module:
Step 1: Farmer Login and Application Process through the "Mahavistaar-AI Application"
a) First, download and install the "Mahavistaar-AI Application" from the "Google Play Store" on your mobile.
b) After entering the application, enter your registered Farmer ID.
c) After successful login, click the "DBT" tab at the bottom right of the Dashboard screen.
d) Upon clicking, click the "NDKSP (PoCRA)" tab.
e) To avail benefits for various items under individual components, click the "Click Here" link at the end of this screen to apply.
f) Following this, your NDKSP (PoCRA) project dashboard screen will be available.
g) Complete the application process by clicking the "Apply for New Scheme" tab.
Step 2: Farmer Login and application Process through the "Project's DBT Web Portal"
a) Visit to "https://mahapocra.gov.in/mr/applications" NDKSP 2.0 website
b) After entering the webpage of Farmer login, enter your registered Farmer ID.
c) After successful login, dashboard screen will be available.
d) Complete the application process by clicking the "Apply for New Scheme" tab.

*Source Url*:
https://mahapocra.gov.in/documents/Inland_Fishery_Guideline_NDKSP_2.0.pdf
